newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel 1997 budget cut clears final hurdle.
newsitem.headline: Israel 1997 budget cut clears final hurdle.

text.p: The Israeli parliament's finance committee on Wednesday approved, by a majority of one, an 800 million shekel ($226.6 million) cut in the government's 1997 budget, the committee secretary said.
The committee's approval was the final hurdle for the cut, which will enable the government to meet its 1997 budget deficit target of 9.7 billion shekels or 2.8 percent of gross domestic product.
The cut affects all ministry budgets, with the lion's share coming from defence and education spending.

The 800 million shekel reduction in the state budget includes 180 million shekels now earmarked to fund transfers of U.S. aid from Israel to Jordan in accordance with an agreement between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and U.S. President Bill Clinton.

Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman withdrew his budget proposal at the last minute on Sunday when it became clear that certain members of the government coalition objected to cuts in the education and social welfare budgets.
Neeman resubmitted the proposal for a vote on Wednesday after lobbying legislators to support the cut and guarantee a majority in the committee.
The latest round of budget trimming is in addition to seven billion shekels in cuts and revenue raising measures already implemented.
Later on Wednesday, the cabinet is due to resume discussion of the 1998 budget and the Treasury's package of around 100 reforms aimed at reviving Israel's stagnant economy next year.
The Treasury plan, unveiled last week, includes measures for privatisation, capital market reform and foreign currency liberalisation.
Trade unions have threatened industrial action if recommendations concerning privatisation and increased competition for state monopolies are approved.

"Non-implementation of the steps presented here will lead to an economic standstill with an increase in unemployment up to some 11 percent," Finance Ministry director general Shmuel Slavin told the cabinet on Sunday.
Israel's unemployment was 7.3 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
For 1998 the Treasury has set a budget of 164.4 billion shekels, from which it now proposes to cut about 2.5 billion shekels.
It has asked the cabinet to set next year's budget deficit at 8.5 billion shekels, or 2.4 percent of gross domestic product.
The cabinet will meet on August 31 to vote on the budget before sending it to parliament for approval by year end.
